advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_DELAY.comment:
建议使用默认值；若有特殊用途，可使用以下定义
不要启用探针可能不理解的设置。克隆品可能无法识别
高级命令。

注意：若探针未伸出，请执行“复位”和“自检”，然后检查
棕、红、橙线的接线。

注意：若探针的触发信号未被识别，通常是因为
黑线和白线需要对调。它们不像真正的开关那样“可互换”。
因此请先检查接线。

适用于所有 BLTouch 及克隆探针的设置：
安全：探针需要时间来识别命令。
最小命令延迟 (ms)。如有需要请启用并增大。
advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_DELAY.name: BLTOUCH_DELAY

advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_FORCE_MODE_SET.comment:
安全：连接电压模式未知的探针时启用。
V3.0：在 Marlin 启动时将探针设为上方所选模式。3.0 上的 5V 模式需要此项
V3.1：在 Marlin 启动时强制将模式未知的探针设为所选模式（= 写入探针 EEPROM）
为延长探针寿命，使用一次后请关闭并重新烧录。
advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_FORCE_MODE_SET.name: BLTOUCH_FORCE_MODE_SET

advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_FORCE_SW_MODE.comment:
适用于 BLTOUCH Classic 1.2、1.3 或 BLTouch Smart 1.0、2.0、2.2、3.0、3.1 及大多数克隆品的设置：
功能：伸出后切换到 SW 模式。可使输出脉冲更长。在某些
特殊情况下有用，例如有噪声或滤波的输入配置。
advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_FORCE_SW_MODE.name: BLTOUCH_FORCE_SW_MODE

advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_HS_MODE.comment:
启用“高速”探测选项。
危险：若探针有时失灵请禁用。仅适用于稳定且调试良好的系统。
此功能为 Z 轴移动极快的 Delta 机设计；但高速笛卡尔机
可能也能使用。若机器无法足够快地抬起 Z，BLTouch 可能进入报警状态。

在此设置默认状态，可用 'M401 S' 或界面更改，M500 保存，M502 复位。
advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_HS_MODE.name: BLTOUCH_HS_MODE

advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_LCD_VOLTAGE_MEN.comment: 安全：在 LCD 菜单中启用电压模式设置。
advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_LCD_VOLTAGE_MEN.name: BLTOUCH_LCD_VOLTAGE_MENU

advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_SET_5V_MODE.comment:
危险：除非连接到 5V 兼容控制器，否则不要启用 5V 模式！
V3.0 或 3.1：在 Marlin 启动时将默认模式设为 5V 模式。
若禁用，3.0 上硬编码默认为 OD 模式
启动时 Marlin 会将其 EEPROM 与此值比较。若所选模式
不同，将在初始化时完成一次模式设置的 EEPROM 写入。
无论如何，使用下方选项强制向 V3.1 探针写入 EEPROM。
advanced|bltouch|BLTOUCH_SET_5V_MODE.name: BLTOUCH_SET_5V_MODE

advanced|cnc|SPINDLE_FEATURE.comment:
Spindle & Laser control

Add the M3, M4, and M5 commands to turn the spindle/laser on and off, and
to set spindle speed, spindle direction, and laser power.

SuperPid is a router/spindle speed controller used in the CNC milling community.
Marlin can be used to turn the spindle on and off. It can also be used to set
the spindle speed from 5,000 to 30,000 RPM.

You'll need to select a pin for the ON/OFF function and optionally choose a 0-5V
hardware PWM pin for the speed control and a pin for the rotation direction.

See https://marlinfw.org/docs/configuration/2.0.9/laser_spindle.html for more config details.

advanced|extras|DUAL_X_CARRIAGE.comment:
双 X 滑架

此设置有两个可独立移动的 X 滑架，各自配有一个挤出机。
滑架可用于用两种颜色或材料打印物体，或在
“复制模式”下同时打印两个相同或 X 镜像的物体。
未使用的滑架会自动停放以防漏料。
X1 为左滑架，X2 为右滑架。它们在 X 轴的两端停放和归位。
默认 X2 步进电机分配到主板上第一个未使用的 E 插座。

可用 M605 S<mode> 选择以下双 X 滑架模式：

0 : (FULL_CONTROL) 切片器完全控制两个 X 滑架，只要支持双 X 滑架
即可获得最佳移动效果。(M605 S0)

1 : (AUTO_PARK) 固件在换刀时自动停放和收回 X 滑架，
因此无需额外的切片器支持。(M605 S1)

2 : (DUPLICATION) 固件使第二个 X 滑架和挤出机与第一个
X 滑架和挤出机同步移动，同时打印同一物体的 2 份副本。
用 M605 S2 X[offs] R[deg] 设置恒定 X 偏移和温度差，
随后用 M605 S2 启动复制移动。

3 : (MIRRORED) 受 Formbot/Vivedino 启发的镜像模式，第二个挤出机复制
第一个的移动，但第二个挤出机在 X 轴上反向。
用 M605 S2 X[offs] R[deg] 设置初始 X 偏移和温度差，
随后用 M605 S3 启动镜像移动。
advanced|extras|DUAL_X_CARRIAGE.name: DUAL_X_CARRIAGE

200 : Minimum for A4988 drivers
400 : Minimum for A5984 drivers
500 : Minimum for LV8729 drivers (guess, no info in datasheet)
650 : Minimum for DRV8825 drivers
1500 : Minimum for TB6600 drivers (guess, no info in datasheet)
15000 : Minimum for TB6560 drivers (guess, no info in datasheet)

2 : Minimum for DRV8825 stepper drivers

advanced|extruder|LIN_ADVANCE.comment:
Linear Pressure Control v1.5

Assumption: advance [steps] = k * (delta velocity [steps/s])
K=0 means advance disabled.

NOTE: K values for LIN_ADVANCE 1.5 differ from earlier versions!

Set K around 0.22 for 3mm PLA Direct Drive with ~6.5cm between the drive gear and heatbreak.
Larger K values will be needed for flexible filament and greater distances.
If this algorithm produces a higher speed offset than the extruder can handle (compared to E jerk)
print acceleration will be reduced during the affected moves to keep within the limit.

See https://marlinfw.org/docs/features/lin_advance.html for full instructions.

advanced|i2cbus|EXPERIMENTAL_I2CBUS.comment:
TWI/I2C BUS

This feature is an EXPERIMENTAL feature so it shall not be used on production
machines. Enabling this will allow you to send and receive I2C data from slave
devices on the bus.

; Example #1
; This macro send the string "Marlin" to the slave device with address 0x63 (99)
; It uses multiple M260 commands with one B<base 10> arg
M260 A99  ; Target slave address
M260 B77  ; M
M260 B97  ; a
M260 B114 ; r
M260 B108 ; l
M260 B105 ; i
M260 B110 ; n
M260 S1   ; Send the current buffer

; Example #2
; Request 6 bytes from slave device with address 0x63 (99)
M261 A99 B5

; Example #3
; Example serial output of a M261 request
echo:i2c-reply: from:99 bytes:5 data:hello

advanced|lcd|SDCARD_SORT_ALPHA.comment:
Sort SD file listings in alphabetical order.

With this option enabled, items on SD cards will be sorted
by name for easier navigation.

By default...

- Use the slowest -but safest- method for sorting.
- Folders are sorted to the top.
- The sort key is statically allocated.
- No added G-code (M34) support.
- 40 item sorting limit. (Items after the first 40 are unsorted.)

SD sorting uses static allocation (as set by SDSORT_LIMIT), allowing the
compiler to calculate the worst-case usage and throw an error if the SRAM
limit is exceeded.

- SDSORT_USES_RAM provides faster sorting via a static directory buffer.
- SDSORT_USES_STACK does the same, but uses a local stack-based buffer.
- SDSORT_CACHE_NAMES will retain the sorted file listing in RAM. (Expensive!)
- SDSORT_DYNAMIC_RAM only uses RAM when the SD menu is visible. (Use with caution!)
advanced|lcd|SDCARD_SORT_ALPHA.name: SDCARD_SORT_ALPHA

advanced|lcd|SDSORT_CACHE_NAMES.comment: Keep sorted items in RAM longer for speedy performance. Most expensive option.

advanced|lcd|SDSORT_CACHE_VFATS.comment: Maximum number of 13-byte VFAT entries to use for sorting. Note: Only affects SCROLL_LONG_FILENAMES with SDSORT_CACHE_NAMES but not SDSORT_DYNAMIC_RAM.

advanced|lcd|SDSORT_DYNAMIC_RAM.comment: Use dynamic allocation (within SD menus). Least expensive option. Set SDSORT_LIMIT before use!

Probing Margins

Override PROBING_MARGIN for each side of the build plate
Useful to get probe points to exact positions on targets or
to allow leveling to avoid plate clamps on only specific
sides of the bed. With NOZZLE_AS_PROBE negative values are
allowed, to permit probing outside the bed.

If you are replacing the prior *_PROBE_BED_POSITION options,
LEFT and FRONT values in most cases will map directly over
RIGHT and REAR would be the inverse such as
(X/Y_BED_SIZE - RIGHT/BACK_PROBE_BED_POSITION)

This will allow all positions to match at compilation, however
should the probe position be modified with M851XY then the
probe points will follow. This prevents any change from causing

advanced|motion control|INPUT_SHAPING_X.comment:
Input Shaping -- EXPERIMENTAL

Zero Vibration (ZV) Input Shaping for X and/or Y movements.

This option uses a lot of SRAM for the step buffer. The buffer size is
calculated automatically from SHAPING_FREQ_[XY], DEFAULT_AXIS_STEPS_PER_UNIT,
DEFAULT_MAX_FEEDRATE and ADAPTIVE_STEP_SMOOTHING. The default calculation can
be overridden by setting SHAPING_MIN_FREQ and/or SHAPING_MAX_FEEDRATE.
The higher the frequency and the lower the feedrate, the smaller the buffer.
If the buffer is too small at runtime, input shaping will have reduced
effectiveness during high speed movements.

Tune with M593 D<factor> F<frequency>:

D<factor>    Set the zeta/damping factor. If axes (X, Y, etc.) are not specified, set for all axes.
F<frequency> Set the frequency. If axes (X, Y, etc.) are not specified, set for all axes.
T[map]       Input Shaping type, 0:ZV, 1:EI, 2:2H EI (not implemented yet)
X<1>         Set the given parameters only for the X axis.
Y<1>         Set the given parameters only for the Y axis.
advanced|motion control|INPUT_SHAPING_X.name: INPUT_SHAPING_X

advanced|motion control|SHAPING_FREQ_Y.name: SHAPING_FREQ_Y

advanced|motion control|SHAPING_MAX_STEP.comment: By default the maximum total step rate of the shaped axes. Override to affect SRAM usage.

高温热敏电阻支持

良好读数。这意味着 TEMP_SENSOR_X_RAW_LO_TEMP
很可能在预热过程中加热元件刚开启时被触发，
从而作为安全措施引发 MINTEMP 错误
并强制停止一切。
为规避此限制，我们允许设置一个预热时间（在此期间
不会触发 MINTEMP 错误），并添加一个 min_temp 缓冲区来处理
异常读数。

若要为你的挤出机热敏电阻启用此功能，
请取消注释并在下面的常量中设置大于 0 的值
在触发 MINTEMP 错误之前，允许连续出现
低温错误的次数。（不应超过 10。）
advanced|temperature|MAX_CONSECUTIVE_LOW.name: MAX_CONSECUTIVE_LOW_TEMPERATURE_ERROR_ALLOWED

advanced|temperature|PID_EXTRUSION_SCALI.comment:
向加热器功率添加一个与挤出速度成正比的额外项。

advanced|temperature|PID_EXTRUSION_SCALI.name: PID_EXTRUSION_SCALING

advanced|temperature|PID_FAN_SCALING.comment:
向加热器功率添加一个与风扇转速成正比的额外项。
恰当的 Kf 值应恰好提供足够功率来补偿冷却风扇造成的功率损失。
你可以直接用 DEFAULT_Kf 值添加一个恒定补偿，
也可按照下面的说明获得与转速相关的补偿。

恒定补偿（仅在风扇转速为 0% 和 100% 时使用）
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Kf 值的良好起点来自以下计算：
kf = (power_fan * eff_fan) / power_heater * 255
其中 eff_fan 介于 0.0 和 1.0 之间，取决于风扇效率以及喷嘴/加热器处的气流。

示例：
加热器：40W，风扇：0.1A * 24V = 2.4W，eff_fan = 0.8
Kf = (2.4W * 0.8) / 40W * 255 = 12.24

与风扇转速相关的补偿
--------------------------------
1. 要找到合适的 Kf 值，设置挤出机温度，等待稳定，然后开启风扇（100%）。
确保 PID_FAN_SCALING_LIN_FACTOR 为 0 且未启用 PID_FAN_SCALING_ALTERNATIVE_DEFINITION。
若看到温度下降，重复测试，缓慢增大 Kf 值，直到温度
不再下降。若开启风扇后温度超调，则 Kf 值过大。
2. 记录风扇转速 100% 时的 Kf 值
3. 确定 PID_FAN_SCALING_MIN_SPEED 的合适值，约为风扇开始转动的转速。
4. 针对此风扇转速重复步骤 1 和 2。
5. 启用 PID_FAN_SCALING_ALTERNATIVE_DEFINITION，并将确定的两个 Kf 值填入
PID_FAN_SCALING_AT_FULL_SPEED 和 PID_FAN_SCALING_AT_MIN_SPEED。将最小转速填入 PID_FAN_SCALING_MIN_SPEED
advanced|temperature|PID_FAN_SCALING.name: PID_FAN_SCALING

advanced|temperature|THERMAL_PROTECTION_.comment:
温度保护偏差监测 - 实验性功能
温度传感器卡死时停机。

此功能可能导致某些热稳定的系统停机。务必在各种
条件下进行充分测试。若出现误报请禁用。

此功能确保温度传感器定期更新。若传感器损坏或“卡死”，
或 Marlin 停止读取它们，温度将保持不变而加热器可能仍在供电！
此功能仅监测温度变化，因此应能捕获任何软硬件问题。

默认使用上述 THERMAL_PROTECTION_*_PERIOD 常量作为时间窗口，在此窗口内
必须至少发生一次温度变化，以表明传感器轮询正常。若任何被监测的
加热器温度在此期间完全不变（甚至没有微小变化），则
触发温度故障错误并停止打印机。

非常稳定的加热器可能产生误报并停机。此时可尝试稍微增大
相应的 THERMAL_PROTECTION_*_PERIOD 常量。请记住，不应让不受控的加热
持续超过一两分钟。

禁用此功能前，请务必区分误报与真正的传感器问题。若
重启后加热器温度甚至略高于预期，可能存在真正的
温度故障。请在上位机中查看温度曲线是否有异常突起。
advanced|temperature|THERMAL_PROTECTION_.name: THERMAL_PROTECTION_VARIANCE_MONITOR

advanced|temperature|THERMOCOUPLE_MAX_ER.comment:
热电偶传感器对噪声相当敏感。任何在传感器导线上引入的噪声，
例如与步进电机导线并行敷设所产生的噪声，
都可能使热电偶传感器报出虚假错误。此值表示在错误
被上报之前允许连续出现的错误次数。
这让我们可以忽略间歇性错误状况，同时
仍能检测到真正的故障，真正的故障应表现为
来自传感器的持续错误流。

将此值设为 0 表示一出现首个错误即报错。
advanced|temperature|THERMOCOUPLE_MAX_ER.name: THERMOCOUPLE_MAX_ERRORS

basic|calibrate|AUTO_BED_LEVELING_3POINT.comment:
Choose one of the options below to enable G29 Bed Leveling. The parameters
and behavior of G29 will change depending on your selection.

If using a Probe for Z Homing, enable Z_SAFE_HOMING also!

- AUTO_BED_LEVELING_3POINT
Probe 3 arbitrary points on the bed (that aren't collinear)
You specify the XY coordinates of all 3 points.
The result is a single tilted plane. Best for a flat bed.

- AUTO_BED_LEVELING_LINEAR
Probe several points in a grid.
You specify the rectangle and the density of sample points.
The result is a single tilted plane. Best for a flat bed.

- AUTO_BED_LEVELING_BILINEAR
Probe several points in a grid.
You specify the rectangle and the density of sample points.
The result is a mesh, best for large or uneven beds.

- AUTO_BED_LEVELING_UBL (Unified Bed Leveling)
A comprehensive bed leveling system combining the features and benefits
of other systems. UBL also includes integrated Mesh Generation, Mesh
Validation and Mesh Editing systems.

- MESH_BED_LEVELING
Probe a grid manually
The result is a mesh, suitable for large or uneven beds. (See BILINEAR.)
For machines without a probe, Mesh Bed Leveling provides a method to
perform leveling in steps so you can manually adjust the Z height at each
grid-point. With an LCD controller the process is guided step-by-step.
basic|calibrate|AUTO_BED_LEVELING_3POINT.name: AUTO_BED_LEVELING_3POINT

basic|calibrate|SKEW_CORRECTION.comment:
Bed Skew Compensation

This feature corrects for misalignment in the XYZ axes.

Take the following steps to get the bed skew in the XY plane:
1. Print a test square (e.g., https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2563185)
2. For XY_DIAG_AC measure the diagonal A to C
3. For XY_DIAG_BD measure the diagonal B to D
4. For XY_SIDE_AD measure the edge A to D

Marlin automatically computes skew factors from these measurements.
Skew factors may also be computed and set manually:

- Compute AB     : SQRT(2*AC*AC+2*BD*BD-4*AD*AD)/2
- XY_SKEW_FACTOR : TAN(PI/2-ACOS((AC*AC-AB*AB-AD*AD)/(2*AB*AD)))

If desired, follow the same procedure for XZ and YZ.
Use these diagrams for reference:

Y                     Z                     Z
^     B-------C       ^     B-------C       ^     B-------C
|    /       /        |    /       /        |    /       /
|   /       /         |   /       /         |   /       /
|  A-------D          |  A-------D          |  A-------D
+-------------->X     +-------------->X     +-------------->Y
XY_SKEW_FACTOR        XZ_SKEW_FACTOR        YZ_SKEW_FACTOR
basic|calibrate|SKEW_CORRECTION.name: SKEW_CORRECTION

CHAMBER_LIMIT_SWITCHING will enable hysteresis.

The PID frequency will be the same as the extruder PWM.
If PID_dT is the default, and correct for the hardware/configuration, that
means 7.689Hz, which is fine for driving a square wave into a resistive load
and does not significantly impact FET heating. This also works fine on a
Fotek SSR-10DA Solid State Relay into a 200W heater. If your configuration is
significantly different than this and you don't understand the issues
involved, don't use chamber PID until someone else verifies that your
hardware works.
basic|chamber temp|PIDTEMPCHAMBER.name: PIDTEMPCHAMBER

basic|chamber temp|PID_AUTOTUNE_MENU.comment: Add PID auto-tuning to the "Advanced Settings" menu. (~250 bytes of flash)
basic|chamber temp|PID_AUTOTUNE_MENU.name: PID_AUTOTUNE_MENU

basic|chamber temp|PID_CHAMBER_DEBUG.comment: Print Chamber PID debug data to the serial port.
basic|chamber temp|PID_CHAMBER_DEBUG.name: PID_CHAMBER_DEBUG

basic|chamber temp|PID_EDIT_MENU.comment: Add PID editing to the "Advanced Settings" menu. (~700 bytes of flash)
basic|chamber temp|PID_EDIT_MENU.name: PID_EDIT_MENU

basic|chamber temp|PID_FUNCTIONAL_RANGE.comment: If the temperature difference between the target temperature and the actual temperature is more than PID_FUNCTIONAL_RANGE then the PID will be shut off and the heater will be set to min/max.
basic|chamber temp|PID_FUNCTIONAL_RANGE.name: PID_FUNCTIONAL_RANGE

basic|chamber temp|PID_OPENLOOP.comment: Puts PID in open loop. M104/M140 sets the output power from 0 to PID_MAX
basic|chamber temp|PID_OPENLOOP.name: PID_OPENLOOP

basic|chamber temp|SLOW_PWM_HEATERS.comment: PWM with very low frequency (roughly 0.125Hz=8s) and minimum state time of approximately 1s useful for heaters driven by a relay
basic|chamber temp|SLOW_PWM_HEATERS.name: SLOW_PWM_HEATERS

basic|delta|DEFAULT_SEGMENTS_PER_SECOND.comment:
Make delta curves from many straight lines (linear interpolation).
This is a trade-off between visible corners (not enough segments)
and processor overload (too many expensive sqrt calls).
basic|delta|DEFAULT_SEGMENTS_PER_SECOND.name: DEFAULT_SEGMENTS_PER_SECOND

basic|delta|DELTA.comment: Enable for DELTA kinematics and configure below
basic|delta|DELTA.name: DELTA

basic|delta|DELTA_AUTO_CALIBRATION.comment: G33 Delta Auto-Calibration. Enable EEPROM_SETTINGS to store results.
basic|delta|DELTA_AUTO_CALIBRATION.name: DELTA_AUTO_CALIBRATION

basic|delta|DELTA_CALIBRATION_DEFAULT_PO.comment: Default number of probe points : n*n (1 -> 7)
basic|delta|DELTA_CALIBRATION_DEFAULT_PO.name: DELTA_CALIBRATION_DEFAULT_POINTS

basic|delta|DELTA_CALIBRATION_MENU.comment:
Delta calibration menu
Add three-point calibration to the MarlinUI menu.
See http://minow.blogspot.com/index.html#4918805519571907051
basic|delta|DELTA_CALIBRATION_MENU.name: DELTA_CALIBRATION_MENU

basic|delta|DELTA_ENDSTOP_ADJ.comment: Get these values from G33 auto calibrate
basic|delta|DELTA_ENDSTOP_ADJ.name: DELTA_ENDSTOP_ADJ

basic|delta|DELTA_HEIGHT.comment: (mm) Get this value from G33 auto calibrate
basic|delta|DELTA_HEIGHT.name: DELTA_HEIGHT

basic|delta|DELTA_HOME_TO_SAFE_ZONE.comment: After homing move down to a height where XY movement is unconstrained
basic|delta|DELTA_HOME_TO_SAFE_ZONE.name: DELTA_HOME_TO_SAFE_ZONE

basic|delta|DELTA_RADIUS.comment: (mm) Get this value from G33 auto calibrate
basic|delta|DELTA_RADIUS.name: DELTA_RADIUS

basic|delta|DELTA_RADIUS_TRIM_TOWER.comment: Delta radius and diagonal rod adjustments (mm)
basic|delta|DELTA_RADIUS_TRIM_TOWER.name: DELTA_RADIUS_TRIM_TOWER

basic|delta|DELTA_TOWER_ANGLE_TRIM.comment: Get these values from G33 auto calibrate
basic|delta|DELTA_TOWER_ANGLE_TRIM.name: DELTA_TOWER_ANGLE_TRIM

basic|eeprom|DISABLE_M503.comment: Saves ~2700 bytes of flash. Disable for release!
basic|eeprom|DISABLE_M503.name: DISABLE_M503

basic|eeprom|EEPROM_AUTO_INIT.comment: Init EEPROM automatically on any errors.
basic|eeprom|EEPROM_AUTO_INIT.name: EEPROM_AUTO_INIT

basic|eeprom|EEPROM_BOOT_SILENT.comment: Keep M503 quiet and only give errors during first load
basic|eeprom|EEPROM_BOOT_SILENT.name: EEPROM_BOOT_SILENT

basic|eeprom|EEPROM_CHITCHAT.comment: Give feedback on EEPROM commands. Disable to save PROGMEM.
basic|eeprom|EEPROM_CHITCHAT.name: EEPROM_CHITCHAT

basic|eeprom|EEPROM_INIT_NOW.comment: Init EEPROM on first boot after a new build.
basic|eeprom|EEPROM_INIT_NOW.name: EEPROM_INIT_NOW

basic|eeprom|EEPROM_SETTINGS.comment: Persistent storage with M500 and M501
basic|eeprom|EEPROM_SETTINGS.name: EEPROM_SETTINGS

basic|endstops|DETECT_BROKEN_ENDSTOP.comment: Check for stuck or disconnected endstops during homing moves.
basic|endstops|DETECT_BROKEN_ENDSTOP.name: DETECT_BROKEN_ENDSTOP

basic|endstops|ENDSTOPPULLDOWNS.comment: Enable pulldown for all endstops to prevent a floating state
basic|endstops|ENDSTOPPULLDOWNS.name: ENDSTOPPULLDOWNS

basic|endstops|ENDSTOPPULLDOWN_XMIN.comment: Disable ENDSTOPPULLDOWNS to set pulldowns individually
basic|endstops|ENDSTOPPULLDOWN_XMIN.name: ENDSTOPPULLDOWN_XMIN

basic|endstops|ENDSTOPPULLUPS.comment: Enable pullup for all endstops to prevent a floating state
basic|endstops|ENDSTOPPULLUPS.name: ENDSTOPPULLUPS

basic|endstops|ENDSTOPPULLUP_XMIN.comment: Disable ENDSTOPPULLUPS to set pullups individually
basic|endstops|ENDSTOPPULLUP_XMIN.name: ENDSTOPPULLUP_XMIN

basic|endstops|ENDSTOP_INTERRUPTS_FEATUR.comment:
Enable this feature if all enabled endstop pins are interrupt-capable.
This will remove the need to poll the interrupt pins, saving many CPU cycles.
basic|endstops|ENDSTOP_INTERRUPTS_FEATUR.name: ENDSTOP_INTERRUPTS_FEATURE

basic|endstops|ENDSTOP_NOISE_THRESHOLD.comment:
Endstop Noise Threshold

Enable if your probe or endstops falsely trigger due to noise.

- Higher values may affect repeatability or accuracy of some bed probes.
- To fix noise install a 100nF ceramic capacitor in parallel with the switch.
- This feature is not required for common micro-switches mounted on PCBs
based on the Makerbot design, which already have the 100nF capacitor.
basic|endstops|ENDSTOP_NOISE_THRESHOLD.name: ENDSTOP_NOISE_THRESHOLD

basic|endstops|USE_XMIN_PLUG.comment:
Specify here all the endstop connectors that are connected to any endstop or
probe. Almost all printers will be using one per axis. Probes will use one or
more of the extra connectors. Leave undefined any used for non-endstop and
non-probe purposes.
basic|endstops|USE_XMIN_PLUG.name: USE_XMIN_PLUG

basic|endstops|X_MIN_ENDSTOP_HIT_STATE.comment:
Endstop "Hit" State

basic|endstops|X_MIN_ENDSTOP_HIT_STATE.name: X_MIN_ENDSTOP_HIT_STATE

basic|extras|BARICUDA.name: BARICUDA

basic|extruder|DISABLE_E.name: DISABLE_E

basic|extruder|DISABLE_OTHER_EXTRUDERS.name: DISABLE_OTHER_EXTRUDERS

basic|extruder|SINGLENOZZLE.name: SINGLENOZZLE

basic|fans|FAN_SOFT_PWM.comment:
Use software PWM to drive the fan, as for the heaters. This uses a very low
frequency which is not as annoying as with the hardware PWM. On the other
hand, if this frequency is too low, you should also increment SOFT_PWM_SCALE.
basic|fans|FAN_SOFT_PWM.name: FAN_SOFT_PWM

basic|fans|NUM_M106_FANS.comment: Set number of user-controlled fans. Disable to use all board-defined fans.
basic|fans|NUM_M106_FANS.name: NUM_M106_FANS

basic|fans|SOFT_PWM_DITHER.comment:
If SOFT_PWM_SCALE is set to a value higher than 0, dithering can
be used to mitigate the associated resolution loss. If enabled,
some of the PWM cycles are stretched so on average the desired
duty cycle is attained.
basic|fans|SOFT_PWM_DITHER.name: SOFT_PWM_DITHER

basic|fans|SOFT_PWM_SCALE.comment:
Incrementing this by 1 will double the software PWM frequency,
affecting heaters, and the fan if FAN_SOFT_PWM is enabled.
However, control resolution will be halved for each increment;
at zero value, there are 128 effective control positions.
basic|fans|SOFT_PWM_SCALE.name: SOFT_PWM_SCALE

basic|geometry|FILAMENT_MOTION_SENSOR.comment:
Enable this option to use an encoder disc that toggles the runout pin
as the filament moves. (Be sure to set FILAMENT_RUNOUT_DISTANCE_MM
large enough to avoid false positives.)
basic|geometry|FILAMENT_MOTION_SENSOR.name: FILAMENT_MOTION_SENSOR

basic|geometry|FILAMENT_RUNOUT_DISTANCE_.comment:
After a runout is detected, continue printing this length of filament
before executing the runout script. Useful for a sensor at the end of
a feed tube. Requires 4 bytes SRAM per sensor, plus 4 bytes overhead.
basic|geometry|FILAMENT_RUNOUT_DISTANCE_.name: FILAMENT_RUNOUT_DISTANCE_MM

basic|geometry|FILAMENT_RUNOUT_SCRIPT.comment:
Commands to execute on filament runout.
With multiple runout sensors use the %c placeholder for the current tool in
commands (e.g., "M600 T%c") NOTE: After 'M412 H1' the host handles filament
runout and this script does not apply.
basic|geometry|FILAMENT_RUNOUT_SCRIPT.name: FILAMENT_RUNOUT_SCRIPT

basic|geometry|FILAMENT_RUNOUT_SENSOR.comment:
Filament Runout Sensors
Mechanical or opto endstops are used to check for the presence of filament.

IMPORTANT: Runout will only trigger if Marlin is aware that a print job is
running. Marlin knows a print job is running when:
1. Running a print job from media started with M24.
2. The Print Job Timer has been started with M75.
3. The heaters were turned on and PRINTJOB_TIMER_AUTOSTART is enabled.

RAMPS-based boards use SERVO3_PIN for the first runout sensor.
For other boards you may need to define FIL_RUNOUT_PIN, FIL_RUNOUT2_PIN, etc.
basic|geometry|FILAMENT_RUNOUT_SENSOR.name: FILAMENT_RUNOUT_SENSOR

basic|geometry|FIL_MOTION1_STATE.comment: Override individually if the motion sensors vary
basic|geometry|FIL_MOTION1_STATE.name: FIL_MOTION1_STATE

basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT1_STATE.comment: Override individually if the runout sensors vary
basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT1_STATE.name: FIL_RUNOUT1_STATE

basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT_ENABLED_DEFAUL.comment: Enable the sensor on startup. Override with M412 followed by M500.
basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT_ENABLED_DEFAUL.name: FIL_RUNOUT_ENABLED_DEFAULT

basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT_PULLDOWN.comment: Use internal pulldown for filament runout pins.
basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT_PULLDOWN.name: FIL_RUNOUT_PULLDOWN

basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT_PULLUP.comment: Use internal pullup for filament runout pins.
basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT_PULLUP.name: FIL_RUNOUT_PULLUP

basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT_STATE.comment: Pin state indicating that filament is NOT present.
basic|geometry|FIL_RUNOUT_STATE.name: FIL_RUNOUT_STATE

basic|geometry|MAX_SOFTWARE_ENDSTOPS.comment: Max software endstops constrain movement within maximum coordinate bounds
basic|geometry|MAX_SOFTWARE_ENDSTOPS.name: MAX_SOFTWARE_ENDSTOPS

basic|geometry|MIN_SOFTWARE_ENDSTOPS.comment:
Software Endstops

- Prevent moves outside the set machine bounds.
- Individual axes can be disabled, if desired.
- X and Y only apply to Cartesian robots.
- Use 'M211' to set software endstops on/off or report current state
Min software endstops constrain movement within minimum coordinate bounds
basic|geometry|MIN_SOFTWARE_ENDSTOPS.name: MIN_SOFTWARE_ENDSTOPS

basic|geometry|NUM_MOTION_SENSORS.comment: Number of sensors, up to one per extruder. Define a FIL_MOTION#_PIN for each.
basic|geometry|NUM_MOTION_SENSORS.name: NUM_MOTION_SENSORS

basic|geometry|NUM_RUNOUT_SENSORS.comment: Number of sensors, up to one per extruder. Define a FIL_RUNOUT#_PIN for each.
basic|geometry|NUM_RUNOUT_SENSORS.name: NUM_RUNOUT_SENSORS

basic|geometry|SOFT_ENDSTOPS_MENU_ITEM.comment: Enable/Disable software endstops from the LCD
basic|geometry|SOFT_ENDSTOPS_MENU_ITEM.name: SOFT_ENDSTOPS_MENU_ITEM

basic|geometry|WATCH_ALL_RUNOUT_SENSORS.comment: Execute runout script on any triggering sensor, not only for the active extruder. This is automatically enabled for MIXING_EXTRUDERs.
basic|geometry|WATCH_ALL_RUNOUT_SENSORS.name: WATCH_ALL_RUNOUT_SENSORS

basic|geometry|X_BED_SIZE.comment: The size of the printable area
basic|geometry|X_BED_SIZE.name: X_BED_SIZE

basic|geometry|X_MIN_POS.comment:
Travel limits (linear=mm, rotational=°) after homing, corresponding to
endstop positions.
basic|geometry|X_MIN_POS.name: X_MIN_POS

basic|homing|BED_CENTER_AT_0_0.comment: The center of the bed is at (X=0, Y=0)
basic|homing|BED_CENTER_AT_0_0.name: BED_CENTER_AT_0_0

basic|homing|HOME_AFTER_DEACTIVATE.comment: Require rehoming after steppers are deactivated. Also enable NO_MOTION_BEFORE_HOMING for extra safety.
basic|homing|HOME_AFTER_DEACTIVATE.name: HOME_AFTER_DEACTIVATE

basic|homing|MANUAL_X_HOME_POS.comment:
Manually set the home position. Leave these undefined for automatic settings.
For DELTA this is the top-center of the Cartesian print volume.
basic|homing|MANUAL_X_HOME_POS.name: MANUAL_X_HOME_POS

basic|homing|NO_MOTION_BEFORE_HOMING.comment: Inhibit movement until all axes have been homed. Also enable HOME_AFTER_DEACTIVATE for extra safety.
basic|homing|NO_MOTION_BEFORE_HOMING.name: NO_MOTION_BEFORE_HOMING

basic|homing|VALIDATE_HOMING_ENDSTOPS.comment: Validate that endstops are triggered on homing moves
basic|homing|VALIDATE_HOMING_ENDSTOPS.name: VALIDATE_HOMING_ENDSTOPS

basic|homing|Z_AFTER_HOMING.comment: (mm) Height to move to after homing Z
basic|homing|Z_AFTER_HOMING.name: Z_AFTER_HOMING

basic|homing|Z_HOMING_HEIGHT.comment: (mm) Minimal Z height before homing (G28) for Z clearance above the bed, clamps, ... Be sure to have this much clearance over your Z_MAX_POS to prevent grinding.
basic|homing|Z_HOMING_HEIGHT.name: Z_HOMING_HEIGHT

basic|homing|Z_IDLE_HEIGHT.comment:
Set Z_IDLE_HEIGHT if the Z-Axis moves on its own when steppers are disabled.
- Use a low value (i.e., Z_MIN_POS) if the nozzle falls down to the bed.
- Use a large value (i.e., Z_MAX_POS) if the bed falls down, away from the
nozzle.
basic|homing|Z_IDLE_HEIGHT.name: Z_IDLE_HEIGHT

basic|homing|Z_SAFE_HOMING.comment:
Use "Z Safe Homing" to avoid homing with a Z probe outside the bed area.

- Moves the Z probe (or nozzle) to a defined XY point before Z homing.
- Allows Z homing only when XY positions are known and trusted.
- If stepper drivers sleep, XY homing may be required again before Z homing.
basic|homing|Z_SAFE_HOMING.name: Z_SAFE_HOMING

basic|homing|Z_SAFE_HOMING_POINT_ABSOLUT.comment: Ignore home offsets (M206) for Z homing position
basic|homing|Z_SAFE_HOMING_POINT_ABSOLUT.name: Z_SAFE_HOMING_POINT_ABSOLUTE

basic|host|BUSY_WHILE_HEATING.comment: Some hosts require "busy" messages even during heating
basic|host|BUSY_WHILE_HEATING.name: BUSY_WHILE_HEATING

basic|host|DEFAULT_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL.comment: Number of seconds between "busy" messages. Set with M113.
basic|host|DEFAULT_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL.name: DEFAULT_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL

basic|host|HOST_KEEPALIVE_FEATURE.comment: Disable this if your host doesn't like keepalive messages
basic|host|HOST_KEEPALIVE_FEATURE.name: HOST_KEEPALIVE_FEATURE

basic|host|PRINTJOB_TIMER_AUTOSTART.comment:
Print Job Timer

Automatically start and stop the print job timer on
M104/M109/M140/M190/M141/M191. The print job timer will only be stopped if
the bed/chamber target temp is below BED_MINTEMP/CHAMBER_MINTEMP.

M104 (hotend, no wait)  - high temp = none,        low temp = stop timer
M109 (hotend, wait)     - high temp = start timer, low temp = stop timer
M140 (bed, no wait)     - high temp = none,        low temp = stop timer
M190 (bed, wait)        - high temp = start timer, low temp = none
M141 (chamber, no wait) - high temp = none,        low temp = stop timer
M191 (chamber, wait)    - high temp = start timer, low temp = none

For M104/M109, high temp is anything over EXTRUDE_MINTEMP / 2.
For M140/M190, high temp is anything over BED_MINTEMP.
For M141/M191, high temp is anything over CHAMBER_MINTEMP.

The timer can also be controlled with the following commands:

M75 - Start the print job timer
M76 - Pause the print job timer
M77 - Stop the print job timer
basic|host|PRINTJOB_TIMER_AUTOSTART.name: PRINTJOB_TIMER_AUTOSTART

basic|hotend temp|BANG_MAX.name: BANG_MAX

basic|hotend temp|DEFAULT_Kp_LIST.comment:
Specify up to one value per hotend here, according to your setup.
If there are fewer values, the last one applies to the remaining hotends.
basic|hotend temp|DEFAULT_Kp_LIST.name: DEFAULT_Kp_LIST

basic|hotend temp|PIDTEMP.comment: See the PID Tuning Guide at https://reprap.org/wiki/PID_Tuning
basic|hotend temp|PIDTEMP.name: PIDTEMP

basic|hotend temp|PID_DEBUG.comment: Print PID debug data to the serial port. Use 'M303 D' to toggle activation.
basic|hotend temp|PID_DEBUG.name: PID_DEBUG

basic|hotend temp|PID_K1.comment: Smoothing factor within any PID loop
basic|hotend temp|PID_K1.name: PID_K1

basic|hotend temp|PID_MAX.comment: Limits current to nozzle while PID is active (see PID_FUNCTIONAL_RANGE below); 255=full current
basic|hotend temp|PID_MAX.name: PID_MAX

basic|hotend temp|PID_PARAMS_PER_HOTEND.comment: Use separate PID parameters for each extruder (useful for mismatched extruders) Set/get with G-code: M301 E[extruder number, 0-2]
basic|hotend temp|PID_PARAMS_PER_HOTEND.name: PID_PARAMS_PER_HOTEND

basic|info|CUSTOM_VERSION_FILE.comment: 相对于根目录的路径（不加引号）
basic|info|CUSTOM_VERSION_FILE.name: CUSTOM_VERSION_FILE

basic|interface|DISPLAY_CHARSET_HD44780.comment:
LCD Character Set

Note: This option is NOT applicable to Graphical Displays.

All character-based LCDs provide ASCII plus one of these
language extensions:

- JAPANESE ... the most common
- WESTERN  ... with more accented characters
- CYRILLIC ... for the Russian language

To determine the language extension installed on your controller:

- Compile and upload with LCD_LANGUAGE set to 'test'
- Click the controller to view the LCD menu
- The LCD will display Japanese, Western, or Cyrillic text

See https://marlinfw.org/docs/development/lcd_language.html
basic|interface|DISPLAY_CHARSET_HD44780.name: DISPLAY_CHARSET_HD44780

basic|interface|ENCODER_NOISE_FILTER.comment:
Encoder EMI Noise Filter
This option increases encoder samples to filter out phantom encoder clicks
caused by EMI noise.
basic|interface|ENCODER_NOISE_FILTER.name: ENCODER_NOISE_FILTER

basic|interface|ENCODER_PULSES_PER_STEP.comment:
ENCODER SETTINGS
This option overrides the default number of encoder pulses needed to
produce one step. Should be increased for high-resolution encoders.
basic|interface|ENCODER_PULSES_PER_STEP.name: ENCODER_PULSES_PER_STEP

basic|interface|ENCODER_STEPS_PER_MENU_I.comment:
Use this option to override the number of step signals required to
move between next/prev menu items.
basic|interface|ENCODER_STEPS_PER_MENU_I.name: ENCODER_STEPS_PER_MENU_ITEM

basic|interface|INDIVIDUAL_AXIS_HOMING_M.comment:
Individual Axis Homing
Add individual axis homing items (Home X, Home Y, and Home Z) to the LCD
menu.
basic|interface|INDIVIDUAL_AXIS_HOMING_M.name: INDIVIDUAL_AXIS_HOMING_MENU

basic|interface|LCD_FEEDBACK_FREQUENCY_D.comment:
The duration and frequency for the UI feedback sound.
Set these to 0 to disable audio feedback in the LCD menus.
Note: Test audio output with the G-Code:
M300 S<frequency Hz> P<duration ms>
basic|interface|LCD_FEEDBACK_FREQUENCY_D.name: LCD_FEEDBACK_FREQUENCY_DURATION_MS

basic|interface|LCD_LANGUAGE.comment:
LCD LANGUAGE

Select the language to display on the LCD. These languages are available:

en, an, bg, ca, cz, da, de, el, el_CY, es, eu, fi, fr, gl, hr, hu, it,
jp_kana, ko_KR, nl, pl, pt, pt_br, ro, ru, sk, sv, tr, uk, vi, zh_CN, zh_TW
basic|interface|LCD_LANGUAGE.name: LCD_LANGUAGE

basic|interface|NO_LCD_MENUS.comment:
LCD Menu Items

Disable all menus and only display the Status Screen, or
just remove some extraneous menu items to recover space.
basic|interface|NO_LCD_MENUS.name: NO_LCD_MENUS

basic|interface|REVERSE_ENCODER_DIRECTIO.comment:
Encoder Direction Options

Test your encoder's behavior first with both options disabled.

Reversed Value Edit and Menu Nav? Enable REVERSE_ENCODER_DIRECTION.
Reversed Menu Navigation only?    Enable REVERSE_MENU_DIRECTION.
Reversed Value Editing only?      Enable BOTH options.

Set this option if CLOCKWISE causes values to DECREASE

This option reverses the encoder direction for navigating LCD menus.
If CLOCKWISE normally moves DOWN this makes it go UP.

basic|interface|REVERSE_SELECT_DIRECTION.comment:
This option reverses the encoder direction for Select Screen.
If CLOCKWISE normally moves LEFT this makes it go RIGHT.
If CLOCKWISE normally moves RIGHT this makes it go LEFT.
basic|interface|REVERSE_SELECT_DIRECTION.name: REVERSE_SELECT_DIRECTION

basic|lcd|ANYCUBIC_LCD_GCODE_EXT.name: ANYCUBIC_LCD_GCODE_EXT

basic|lcd|ANYCUBIC_LCD_I3MEGA.name: ANYCUBIC_LCD_I3MEGA

basic|lights|PRINTER_EVENT_LEDS.comment:
Printer Event LEDs

During printing, the LEDs will reflect the printer status:

- Gradually change from blue to violet as the heated bed gets to target temp
- Gradually change from violet to red as the hotend gets to temperature
- Change to white to illuminate work surface
- Change to green once print has finished
- Turn off after the print has finished and the user has pushed a button
basic|lights|PRINTER_EVENT_LEDS.name: PRINTER_EVENT_LEDS
basic|lights|PRINTER_EVENT_LEDS.requires: ANY(BLINKM, RGB_LED, RGBW_LED, PCA9632, PCA9533, NEOPIXEL_LED)

basic|lights|RGB_LED.comment:
RGB LED / LED Strip Control

Enable support for an RGB LED connected to 5V digital pins, or
an RGB Strip connected to MOSFETs controlled by digital pins.

Adds the M150 command to set the LED (or LED strip) color.
If pins are PWM capable (e.g., 4, 5, 6, 11) then a range of
luminance values can be set from 0 to 255.
For NeoPixel LED an overall brightness parameter is also available.

=== CAUTION ===
LED Strips require a MOSFET Chip between PWM lines and LEDs,
as the Arduino cannot handle the current the LEDs will require.
Failure to follow this precaution can destroy your Arduino!

NOTE: A separate 5V power supply is required! The NeoPixel LED needs
more current than the Arduino 5V linear regulator can produce.

Requires PWM frequency between 50 <> 100Hz (Check HAL or variant)
Use FAST_PWM_FAN, if possible, to reduce fan noise.
LED Type. Enable only one of the following two options:
basic|lights|RGB_LED.name: RGB_LED

basic|motion|NOZZLE_CLEAN_FEATURE.comment:
Clean Nozzle Feature

Adds the G12 command to perform a nozzle cleaning process.

Parameters:
P  Pattern
S  Strokes / Repetitions
T  Triangles (P1 only)

Patterns:
P0  Straight line (default). This process requires a sponge type material
at a fixed bed location. "S" specifies strokes (i.e. back-forth
motions) between the start / end points.

P1  Zig-zag pattern between (X0, Y0) and (X1, Y1), "T" specifies the
number of zig-zag triangles to do. "S" defines the number of strokes.
Zig-zags are done in whichever is the narrower dimension.
For example, "G12 P1 S1 T3" will execute:

--
|  (X0, Y1) |     /\        /\        /\     | (X1, Y1)
|           |    /  \      /  \      /  \    |
A |           |   /    \    /    \    /    \   |
|           |  /      \  /      \  /      \  |
|  (X0, Y0) | /        \/        \/        \ | (X1, Y0)
--         +--------------------------------+
|________|_________|_________|
T1        T2        T3

P2  Circular pattern with middle at NOZZLE_CLEAN_CIRCLE_MIDDLE.
"R" specifies the radius. "S" specifies the stroke count.
Before starting, the nozzle moves to NOZZLE_CLEAN_START_POINT.

Caveats: The ending Z should be the same as starting Z.
basic|motion|NOZZLE_CLEAN_FEATURE.name: NOZZLE_CLEAN_FEATURE

basic|polar|POLAR.comment:
POLAR Kinematics
developed by Kadir ilkimen for PolarBear CNC and babyBear
https://github.com/kadirilkimen/Polar-Bear-Cnc-Machine
https://github.com/kadirilkimen/babyBear-3D-printer

A polar machine can have different configurations.
This kinematics is only compatible with the following configuration:
X : Independent linear
Y or B : Polar
Z : Independent linear

For example, PolarBear has CoreXZ plus Polar Y or B.

Motion problem for Polar axis near center / origin:

3D printing:
Movements very close to the center of the polar axis take more time than
others. This brief delay results in more material deposition due to the
pressure in the nozzle.

Current Kinematics and feedrate scaling deals with this by making the
movement as fast as possible. It works for slow movements but doesn't work
well with fast ones. A more complicated extrusion compensation must be
implemented.

Ideally, it should estimate that a long rotation near the center is ahead and
will cause unwanted deposition. Therefore it can compensate the extrusion
beforehand.

Laser cutting:
Same thing would be a problem for laser engraving too. As it spends time
rotating at the center point, more likely it will burn more material than it
should. Therefore similar compensation would be implemented for laser-cutting
operations.

Milling:
This shouldn't be a problem for cutting/milling operations.
basic|polar|POLAR.name: POLAR

basic|probes|NOZZLE_TO_PROBE_OFFSET.comment:
Nozzle-to-Probe offsets { X, Y, Z }

X and Y offset
Use a caliper or ruler to measure the distance from the tip of
the Nozzle to the center-point of the Probe in the X and Y axes.

Z offset
- For the Z offset use your best known value and adjust at runtime.
- Common probes trigger below the nozzle and have negative values for Z
offset.
- Probes triggering above the nozzle height are uncommon but do exist. When
using probes such as this, carefully set Z_CLEARANCE_DEPLOY_PROBE and
Z_CLEARANCE_BETWEEN_PROBES to avoid collisions during probing.

Tune and Adjust
-  Probe Offsets can be tuned at runtime with 'M851', LCD menus,
babystepping, etc.
-  PROBE_OFFSET_WIZARD (configuration_adv.h) can be used for setting the Z
offset.

Assuming the typical work area orientation:
- Probe to RIGHT of the Nozzle has a Positive X offset
- Probe to LEFT  of the Nozzle has a Negative X offset
- Probe in BACK  of the Nozzle has a Positive Y offset
- Probe in FRONT of the Nozzle has a Negative Y offset

Some examples:
#define NOZZLE_TO_PROBE_OFFSET { 10, 10, -1 }   // Example "1"
#define NOZZLE_TO_PROBE_OFFSET {-10,  5, -1 }   // Example "2"
#define NOZZLE_TO_PROBE_OFFSET {  5, -5, -1 }   // Example "3"
#define NOZZLE_TO_PROBE_OFFSET {-15,-10, -1 }   // Example "4"

+-- BACK ---+
|    [+]    |
L |        1  | R <-- Example "1" (right+,  back+)
E |  2        | I <-- Example "2" ( left-,  back+)
F |[-]  N  [+]| G <-- Nozzle
T |       3   | H <-- Example "3" (right+, front-)
| 4         | T <-- Example "4" ( left-, front-)
|    [-]    |
O-- FRONT --+

basic|probes|PAUSE_BEFORE_DEPLOY_STOW.name: PAUSE_BEFORE_DEPLOY_STOW

basic|probes|PREHEAT_BEFORE_PROBING.comment: Require minimum nozzle and/or bed temperature for probing
basic|probes|PREHEAT_BEFORE_PROBING.name: PREHEAT_BEFORE_PROBING

basic|probes|PROBE_ACTIVATION_SWITCH.comment:
Probe Activation Switch
A switch indicating proper deployment, or an optical
switch triggered when the carriage is near the bed.
basic|probes|PROBE_ACTIVATION_SWITCH.name: PROBE_ACTIVATION_SWITCH

basic|probes|PROBE_ENABLE_DISABLE.comment:
Probe Enable / Disable
The probe only provides a triggered signal when enabled.
basic|probes|PROBE_ENABLE_DISABLE.name: PROBE_ENABLE_DISABLE

basic|probes|PROBE_MANUALLY.comment:
The "Manual Probe" provides a means to do "Auto" Bed Leveling without a
probe. Use G29 repeatedly, adjusting the Z height at each point with movement
commands or (with LCD_BED_LEVELING) the LCD controller.
basic|probes|PROBE_MANUALLY.name: PROBE_MANUALLY

basic|probes|PROBE_TARE.comment:
Tare Probe (determine zero-point) prior to each probe.
Useful for a strain gauge or piezo sensor that needs to factor out
elements such as cables pulling on the carriage.
basic|probes|PROBE_TARE.name: PROBE_TARE

basic|probes|PROBE_TARE_ONLY_WHILE_INACT.comment: Fail to tare/probe if PROBE_ACTIVATION_SWITCH is active
basic|probes|PROBE_TARE_ONLY_WHILE_INACT.name: PROBE_TARE_ONLY_WHILE_INACTIVE

basic|probes|PROBE_TARE_STATE.comment: State to write pin for tare
basic|probes|PROBE_TARE_STATE.name: PROBE_TARE_STATE

basic|probes|PROBING_ESTEPPERS_OFF.comment: Turn all extruder steppers off when probing
basic|probes|PROBING_ESTEPPERS_OFF.name: PROBING_ESTEPPERS_OFF

basic|probes|PROBING_MARGIN.comment:
Most probes should stay away from the edges of the bed, but
with NOZZLE_AS_PROBE this can be negative for a wider probing area.
basic|probes|PROBING_MARGIN.name: PROBING_MARGIN

basic|probes|PROBING_NOZZLE_TEMP.comment: (°C) Only applies to E0 at this time
basic|probes|PROBING_NOZZLE_TEMP.name: PROBING_NOZZLE_TEMP

basic|probes|PROBING_STEPPERS_OFF.comment: Turn all steppers off (unless needed to hold position) when probing (including extruders)
basic|probes|PROBING_STEPPERS_OFF.name: PROBING_STEPPERS_OFF

basic|probes|PROBING_TOOL.comment: Enable and set to use a specific tool for probing. Disable to allow any tool.
basic|probes|PROBING_TOOL.name: PROBING_TOOL

basic|probes|RACK_AND_PINION_PROBE.comment:
A probe deployed by moving the x-axis, such as the Wilson II's
rack-and-pinion probe designed by Marty Rice.
basic|probes|RACK_AND_PINION_PROBE.name: RACK_AND_PINION_PROBE

basic|probes|SENSORLESS_PROBING.comment:
Use StallGuard2 to probe the bed with the nozzle.
Requires stallGuard-capable Trinamic stepper drivers.
CAUTION: This can damage machines with Z lead screws.
Take extreme care when setting up this feature.
basic|probes|SENSORLESS_PROBING.name: SENSORLESS_PROBING

basic|probes|SLED_DOCKING_OFFSET.comment: The extra distance the X axis must travel to pickup the sled. 0 should be fine but you can push it further if you'd like.
basic|probes|SLED_DOCKING_OFFSET.name: SLED_DOCKING_OFFSET

basic|probes|SMART_EFFECTOR_MOD_PIN.comment: Connect a GPIO pin to the Smart Effector MOD pin
basic|probes|SMART_EFFECTOR_MOD_PIN.name: SMART_EFFECTOR_MOD_PIN

basic|probes|SOLENOID_PROBE.comment: A probe that is deployed and stowed with a solenoid pin (SOL1_PIN)
basic|probes|SOLENOID_PROBE.name: SOLENOID_PROBE

basic|probes|TOUCH_MI_DEPLOY_XPOS.comment: For a magnet on the right side of the bed
basic|probes|TOUCH_MI_DEPLOY_XPOS.name: TOUCH_MI_DEPLOY_XPOS

basic|probes|TOUCH_MI_PROBE.comment:
Touch-MI Probe by hotends.fr

This probe is deployed and activated by moving the X-axis to a magnet at the
edge of the bed. By default, the magnet is assumed to be on the left and
activated by a home. If the magnet is on the right, enable and set
TOUCH_MI_DEPLOY_XPOS to the deploy position.

Also requires: BABYSTEPPING, BABYSTEP_ZPROBE_OFFSET, Z_SAFE_HOMING,
and a minimum Z_HOMING_HEIGHT of 10.
basic|probes|TOUCH_MI_PROBE.name: TOUCH_MI_PROBE

basic|probes|TOUCH_MI_RETRACT_Z.comment: Height at which the probe retracts
basic|probes|TOUCH_MI_RETRACT_Z.name: TOUCH_MI_RETRACT_Z

basic|probes|USE_PROBE_FOR_Z_HOMING.comment: Force the use of the probe for Z-axis homing
basic|probes|USE_PROBE_FOR_Z_HOMING.name: USE_PROBE_FOR_Z_HOMING

basic|probes|WAIT_FOR_BED_HEATER.comment: Wait for bed to heat back up between probes (to improve accuracy)
basic|probes|WAIT_FOR_BED_HEATER.name: WAIT_FOR_BED_HEATER

basic|probes|WAIT_FOR_HOTEND.comment: Wait for hotend to heat back up between probes (to improve accuracy & prevent cold extrude)
basic|probes|WAIT_FOR_HOTEND.name: WAIT_FOR_HOTEND

basic|probes|XY_PROBE_FEEDRATE.comment: X and Y axis travel speed (mm/min) between probes
basic|probes|XY_PROBE_FEEDRATE.name: XY_PROBE_FEEDRATE

basic|probes|X_ENABLE_ON.comment:
For Inverting Stepper Enable Pins (Active Low) use 0, Non Inverting (Active
High) use 1
basic|probes|X_ENABLE_ON.name: X_ENABLE_ON

basic|probes|Z_AFTER_PROBING.comment: Z position after probing is done
basic|probes|Z_AFTER_PROBING.name: Z_AFTER_PROBING

basic|probes|Z_MIN_PROBE_PIN.comment:
Z_MIN_PROBE_PIN

Override this pin only if the probe cannot be connected to
the default Z_MIN_PROBE_PIN for the selected MOTHERBOARD.

- The simplest option is to use a free endstop connector.
- Use 5V for powered (usually inductive) sensors.

- For simple switches...
- Normally-closed (NC) also connect to GND.
- Normally-open (NO) also connect to 5V.
basic|probes|Z_MIN_PROBE_PIN.name: Z_MIN_PROBE_PIN

basic|probes|Z_MIN_PROBE_REPEATABILITY_T.comment: Enable the M48 repeatability test to test probe accuracy
basic|probes|Z_MIN_PROBE_REPEATABILITY_T.name: Z_MIN_PROBE_REPEATABILITY_TEST

basic|probes|Z_MIN_PROBE_USES_Z_MIN_ENDS.comment:
Enable this option for a probe connected to the Z-MIN pin.
The probe replaces the Z-MIN endstop and is used for Z homing.
(Automatically enables USE_PROBE_FOR_Z_HOMING.)
basic|probes|Z_MIN_PROBE_USES_Z_MIN_ENDS.name: Z_MIN_PROBE_USES_Z_MIN_ENDSTOP_PIN

basic|probes|Z_PROBE_ALLEN_KEY.comment:
Allen key retractable z-probe as seen on many Kossel delta printers -
https://reprap.org/wiki/Kossel#Automatic_bed_leveling_probe Deploys by
touching z-axis belt. Retracts by pushing the probe down.
basic|probes|Z_PROBE_ALLEN_KEY.name: Z_PROBE_ALLEN_KEY

basic|probes|Z_PROBE_ALLEN_KEY_DEPLOY_1.comment:
2 or 3 sets of coordinates for deploying and retracting the spring loaded
touch probe on G29, if servo actuated touch probe is not defined. Uncomment
as appropriate for your printer/probe.
basic|probes|Z_PROBE_ALLEN_KEY_DEPLOY_1.name: Z_PROBE_ALLEN_KEY_DEPLOY_1

basic|probes|Z_PROBE_OFFSET_RANGE_MIN.name: Z_PROBE_OFFSET_RANGE_MIN

basic|probes|Z_SERVO_DEACTIVATE_AFTER_ST.name: Z_SERVO_DEACTIVATE_AFTER_STOW

basic|probes|Z_SERVO_MEASURE_ANGLE.name: Z_SERVO_MEASURE_ANGLE

Prevent extrusion if the temperature is below EXTRUDE_MINTEMP.
Add M302 to set the minimum extrusion temperature and/or turn
cold extrusion prevention on and off.

basic|safety|THERMAL_PROTECTION_HOTENDS.name: THERMAL_PROTECTION_HOTENDS

basic|security|PASSWORD_FEATURE.comment:
Password

Set a numerical password for the printer which can be requested:

- When the printer boots up
- Upon opening the 'Print from Media' Menu
- When SD printing is completed or aborted

The following G-codes can be used:

M510 - Lock Printer. Blocks all commands except M511.
M511 - Unlock Printer.
M512 - Set, Change and Remove Password.

If you forget the password and get locked out you'll need to re-flash
the firmware with the feature disabled, reset EEPROM, and (optionally)
re-flash the firmware again with this feature enabled.
basic|security|PASSWORD_FEATURE.name: PASSWORD_FEATURE

basic|security|PASSWORD_LENGTH.comment: (#) Number of digits (1-9). 3 or 4 is recommended
basic|security|PASSWORD_LENGTH.name: PASSWORD_LENGTH

basic|security|PASSWORD_ON_SD_PRINT_MENU.comment: This does not prevent G-codes from running
basic|security|PASSWORD_ON_SD_PRINT_MENU.name: PASSWORD_ON_SD_PRINT_MENU

basic|security|PASSWORD_UNLOCK_GCODE.comment: Unlock with the M511 P<password> command. Disable to prevent brute-force attack.
basic|security|PASSWORD_UNLOCK_GCODE.name: PASSWORD_UNLOCK_GCODE

basic|servos|DEACTIVATE_SERVOS_AFTER_MOV.name: DEACTIVATE_SERVOS_AFTER_MOVE

basic|servos|EDITABLE_SERVO_ANGLES.name: EDITABLE_SERVO_ANGLES

basic|servos|NUM_SERVOS.name: NUM_SERVOS

basic|servos|SERVO_DELAY.comment:

its target angle. 300ms is a good value but you can try less delay. If the
servo can't reach the requested position, increase it.

basic|stepper drivers|X_DRIVER_TYPE.comment:
Stepper Drivers

These settings allow Marlin to tune stepper driver timing and enable advanced
options for stepper drivers that support them. You may also override timing
options in Configuration_adv.h.

Use TMC2208/TMC2208_STANDALONE for TMC2225 drivers and
TMC2209/TMC2209_STANDALONE for TMC2226 drivers.

Options: A4988, A5984, DRV8825, LV8729, TB6560, TB6600, TMC2100,
TMC2130, TMC2130_STANDALONE, TMC2160, TMC2160_STANDALONE,
TMC2208, TMC2208_STANDALONE, TMC2209, TMC2209_STANDALONE,
TMC26X,  TMC26X_STANDALONE,  TMC2660, TMC2660_STANDALONE,
TMC5130, TMC5130_STANDALONE, TMC5160, TMC5160_STANDALONE
